newsitem.title: USA: Israel, Palestinians must discuss map - US.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Palestinians must discuss map - US.

text.p: The United States on Monday refused comment on a reported Israeli proposal to partition the West Bank, saying such issues must be discussed in final status peace negotiations between Israel and Palestinians.

"Our view is that any proposals or comments or plans or maps pertaining to the status of the West Bank and the Gaza strip are properly, and only properly, the preserve of the permanent status talks between the Palestinians and the Israelis," State Departmnent spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

"That's the appropriate forum -- not the State Department briefing; not the White House podium; not in what we say, but in what they say and do," he said. "And so if there is a proposal -- and I gather there is -- then obviously it should be debated between Palestinians and Israelis across the table from one another in permanent status talks."

He was commenting on a Washington Post report that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, a sharp critic of previous Israeli-Palestinian accords, has begun laying the groundwork for his own proposal on conflicting claims to the West Bank.

The newspaper called the proposal "deliberately vague and not discussed yet openly" and said it implied Israeli annexation of the larger part of the territory captured from Jordan in the 1967 MIddle East war.
Word of the map, which the Post said Netanyahu discussed with President Bill Clinton during a visit to Washington in February, came during a difficult time in stalled Israel-Palestinian peace talks.

Tensions between Israel and the Palestinians have been high and have periodically flared into violence since March when Israel began building a Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem, an area seized during the 1967 war. Peace negotiations came to a halt after the construction began.
